risk_tolerance.rationale: Represented the families of intellectuals murdered in Iran's 1998-99 'Chain Murders,' directly implicating government intelligence-ministry agents in her legal filings -- a documented act carrying severe personal risk under Iran's judicial system, corroborated via her own memoir and international press coverage of the case.

independent_thinking.rationale: Continued practicing human-rights and family law after being barred from serving as a judge following the 1979 revolution -- a role she had held under the prior government -- specifically because of her gender under the new legal interpretation, documented via her own memoir's account of this career disruption and her subsequent path.

persistence.rationale: Sustained human-rights legal advocacy in Iran across more than two decades of documented state surveillance, imprisonment threats, and at least one brief detention, continuing to take politically sensitive cases rather than withdrawing into less risky practice.

persuasiveness.rationale: Credited with building sustained international attention to Iranian human-rights cases through her legal work and writing, documented via the 2003 Nobel Peace Prize citation's own framing of her contribution and sustained international media engagement.

impact_motivation.rationale: Consistently focused her legal practice on human-rights and child-custody-law cases with direct, documented public-interest stakes rather than more lucrative or lower-risk legal work, documented via her own account of her case selection.

autonomy_need.rationale: Continued independent legal practice and public advocacy after being removed from her judgeship, rather than leaving the legal profession or the country at that point, documented via her own memoir.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustained direct legal confrontation with Iranian state security institutions over the Chain Murders case and other politically sensitive matters across years, documented via international press coverage; marked dual_edged given the real, ongoing personal and professional cost this is documented to have carried, including eventual exile.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Sustained a direct public advocacy and media role, including international speaking engagements and testimony, following the 2003 Nobel Prize, documented via the extensive public record of her subsequent activity.

achievement_drive.rationale: Sustained legal and human-rights advocacy work across a multi-decade career spanning both a judicial and, after being barred from the bench, a private advocacy path, inferred from the documented continuity and escalating international profile of her work.

collaboration.rationale: Co-founded and worked with Iranian human-rights organizations, including the Defenders of Human Rights Center, suggesting real capacity for sustained institutional collaboration, documented via the organization's own founding record.

proactive_agency.rationale: Self-initiated representation of the Chain Murders victims' families rather than being assigned the cases, documented via her own memoir's account of taking on the case.

planning_orientation.rationale: Co-founded a formal human-rights advocacy organization with defined institutional structure, suggesting some real advance organizational planning.

detail_orientation.rationale: Sustained legal casework, particularly the evidentiary case built against implicated intelligence-ministry agents in the Chain Murders matter, suggests real capacity for exacting, high-stakes documentary work.

adaptability.rationale: Rebuilt her professional life and continued advocacy after being removed from the judiciary and, later, after relocating outside Iran, suggesting real capacity to adapt professionally to major disruption.

leadership_drive.rationale: Founded and led a formal human-rights advocacy organization (the Defenders of Human Rights Center) rather than practicing only as an individual advocate, documented via the organization's own founding record.
